penalties_applied.name: regulated_industry
penalties_applied.reason: Any service that facilitates or advises on cross-border money transfers touches financial services regulation (FCA, BaFin, etc.), payment institution licensing, AML/KYC obligations, and consumer protection rules across multiple jurisdictions. Even a comparison/information tool carries compliance and liability risk.

rationale: International students are individual consumers, not businesses, and the segment is extremely fragmented and hard to reach at low cost; buyer clarity scores low (4) because there is no tight, reachable ICP with budget authority. More critically, any tool operating in the cross-border payments or FX comparison space is squarely in regulated financial services territory across multiple jurisdictions, applying a -1.5 penalty that reflects real compliance costs and legal exposure. Operational autonomy is also limited because accurate, real-time FX and fee data requires licensed data feeds or partnerships. Not viable for this factory.
solution_plan: This would be a comparison tool showing estimated fees and transfer times across providers (Wise, Revolut, bank wire, etc.) for a given tuition payment. Accurate real-time data requires API agreements or web scraping fragile sources; any payment facilitation requires financial licensing. A solo non-technical operator faces real regulatory exposure here, not just technical difficulty. Drop this opportunity.
notes: regulated_industry penalty applied. Total 3.1 below min_total_to_validate. buyer_clarity floor unmet (4, min 6). operational_autonomy floor unmet (5, min 7).
